title: Energy and Society
seo_title: Grade 11 Physics (SPH3U): Energy and Society Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Work, kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy; the law of conservation of energy; power and efficiency; thermal energy and heat; and nuclear energy, half-life and energy sources for society. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Physics, Grade 11, University Preparation (SPH3U), Strand D: Energy and Society)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physics (SPH3U) worksheets on energy: work, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of energy, power, efficiency, heat and nuclear energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy is conserved; it only changes form.
key_sub: W = FΔd, Ek = ½mv², Eg = mgΔh, P = E ÷ t.
body_html:
How to think about it

Work is done when a force moves an object in the direction of the force: W = FΔd cos θ, in joules. Kinetic energy Ek = ½mv² and gravitational potential energy Eg = mgΔh. Without friction, mechanical energy is conserved, so the loss of Eg equals the gain of Ek.

Power is the rate of energy transfer: P = E ÷ t, in watts. Efficiency = useful output energy ÷ input energy × 100%. Heat Q = mcΔT. Nuclear power stations release energy by fission; radioactive waste decays with a fixed half-life.

Example

A 2.0 kg ball falls 5.0 m from rest. Speed just before it lands (no air resistance)?

mgh = ½mv²

v = √(2 × 9.8 × 5.0)

Answer: 9.9 m/s

Example

A motor uses 500 J and does 400 J of useful work. Efficiency?

400 ÷ 500 × 100%

Answer: 80%

Common mistakes

  • Doing work when no displacement happens (holding a heavy box still does no work).
  • Doubling the speed and doubling the kinetic energy: Ek goes up four times.
  • Giving efficiency above 100%.

faq.q: What happens to the energy lost to friction?
faq.a: It becomes thermal energy (and some sound), so the total energy is still conserved.

faq.q: Why is nuclear waste a problem?
faq.a: Some products have long half-lives and stay radioactive for thousands of years.

items.q: Kai pushes a cart with a force of 10 N for 3 m. How much energy is transferred to it? (energy transferred = force × distance)
A force of 20 N moves a body 5 m. The force makes 60° with the displacement. How much work is done?
A force of 50 N moves a body 5 m. The force makes 0° with the displacement. How much work is done?
items.e: W = Fd cos θ = 50 × 5 × cos 0° = 250 J.

items.q: A force of 10 N moves a body 5 m. The force makes 0° with the displacement. How much work is done?
A force of 10 N acts at right angles to the 5 m displacement of a body. How much work does it do?
items.e: cos 90° = 0, so no work is done.

items.q: Which statement is true for a body thrown up (no air resistance)?
c: the sum of kinetic and potential energy stays constant

items.q: Maya pushes a wagon from rest with 25 N for 10 m on a smooth floor (no friction). How much kinetic energy does it gain?
items.e: All the work becomes kinetic energy: 25 × 10 = 250 J.
